title: 한눈에 ⑤ 추측 표현: 비가 올 것 같아요? 왔나 봐요?
objective: You can choose between six guessing expressions by asking "What is my guess based on?" and "How sure am I?"
summary: This sheet compares six Korean ways of guessing by what the guess is based on and how sure you are.

task.title: Choose and complete guesses
task.line: For each item, think about the basis for the guess (a clue, your own knowledge, or a feeling) and the setting, then choose or write the right form.

forms.when: Any basis: something you see, your experience, or just a feeling. Fine for yourself and others, in any style.
forms.means: Medium certainty: 'I think ~ / It looks like ~.'
forms.example: 하늘이 많이 흐리네요. 오후에 비가 올 것 같아요.
forms.exampleMeaning: The sky is really cloudy. I think it's going to rain this afternoon.

forms.when: You just saw or heard a clue, usually about someone else. Don't use it for your own plans.
forms.means: Fairly sure, based on the clue: 'I guess ~ (judging from this).'
forms.example: 민수 씨가 계속 하품을 하네요. 어젯밤에 늦게 잤나 봐요.
forms.exampleMeaning: Minsu keeps yawning. He must have gone to bed late last night.

forms.form: V-는 모양이다 / V-(으)ㄴ 모양이다 (past) / A-(으)ㄴ 모양이다
forms.when: Like -나 보다, it's based on a clue you noticed, about others.
forms.example: 옆집이 아주 조용하네요. 가족들이 여행을 간 모양이에요.
forms.exampleMeaning: It's very quiet next door. The family seems to have gone on a trip.

forms.form: V-는 듯하다 / V-(으)ㄴ 듯하다 (past) / A-(으)ㄴ 듯하다 / -(으)ㄹ 듯하다 (future)
forms.when: Writing, news, reports and formal speech. You rarely hear it with friends.
forms.means: Medium certainty, polite and indirect: 'It appears that ~.'
forms.example: 사람들이 이 제품에 관심이 많은 듯합니다.
forms.exampleMeaning: People appear to be very interested in this product.

forms.when: Casual speech only, based on what you know or remember. It is often used to gently correct the listener.
forms.means: Low to medium certainty: 'Probably ~, I think.' You might be wrong.
forms.example: A: 민지 씨도 오늘 모임에 와요? B: 아마 못 올걸요. 요즘 많이 바쁘대요.
forms.exampleMeaning: A: Is Minji coming to the get-together today too? B: She probably can't. I heard she's really busy these days.

forms.when: A thought or worry that crosses your own mind. It often comes as -나 싶어서 ('so I ...').
forms.means: Low certainty: 'I wonder if ~ / It occurred to me that maybe ~.'
forms.example: 요즘 너무 피곤해서 병원에 가 봐야 하나 싶어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: I've been so tired lately that I'm wondering if I should go see a doctor.

watchOut: 저는 내일 늦게 일어나나 봐요 (X) → 저는 내일 늦게 일어날 것 같아요 (O): You already know your own plans, so don't use -나 보다 for them.
그 식당이 유명하나 봐요 (X) → 그 식당이 유명한가 봐요 (O): Adjectives take -(으)ㄴ가 보다 (and -(으)ㄴ가 싶다).
exercises: Choose the right expression: ① (Talking about your own weekend plan) 저는 이번 주말에 그냥 집에서 (쉴 것 같아요 / 쉬나 봐요). ② (Writing a report) 이번 행사에는 참가자가 작년보다 (늘어날 듯합니다 / 늘어날걸요).
Fill in the blanks with -나 보다 or -(으)ㄴ가 보다 (watch for verb vs. adjective and past): ① 민준 씨가 하루 종일 웃고 있어요. 기분이 (좋다) ____. ② 현관에 처음 보는 신발이 많아요. 손님이 (오다) ____.
You are not 100% sure. Reply with -(으)ㄹ걸요: A: 지훈 씨 아직 사무실에 있어요? B: 아니요, 아까 (퇴근하다) ____.
Complete with -나 싶어서: 친구가 하루 종일 메시지를 안 읽었어요. 혹시 무슨 일이 (생기다) ____ 전화해 봤어요.
Which speaker is guessing from a clue they can see right now, A or B? A: 민호 씨는 다음 달에 이사할걸요. B: 민호 씨 집 앞에 이삿짐 트럭이 있네요. 오늘 이사하나 봐요.
answers: ① 쉴 것 같아요 ② 늘어날 듯합니다
① 좋은가 봐요 ② 왔나 봐요
B (이사하나 봐요: B can see the moving truck)
